userStories.title: Add version field to download checkpoint schema
acceptanceCriteria: DownloadCheckpoint dataclass in src/stages/download_segments.py has a `schema_version: int = 1` field
The `from_dict` classmethod logs a warning when loaded checkpoint has a different schema_version than current
The `to_dict` method includes schema_version in serialized output
Test verifies that loading a checkpoint without schema_version defaults to 1 (backward compat)
Test verifies that loading a checkpoint with mismatched schema_version logs a warning
userStories.notes: Tier: S (small). DONE: Added schema_version: int = 1 to DownloadCheckpoint in src/downloader/checkpoint.py (not download_segments.py as story stated). from_dict defaults missing field to 1, warns on mismatch. to_dict uses asdict() which auto-includes. 5 new tests in test_downloader_checkpoint.py. All 41 tests pass.

userStories.title: Add initialization diagnostics to cookie rotator
acceptanceCriteria: CookieRotator.__init__ logs a summary line: 'Cookie rotator: X/N cookies valid (Y invalid)' after validation
CookieRotator has a `get_status()` method returning a dict with keys: total, valid, invalid, cooldown, exhausted
When `continue_on_partial=True` and some cookies fail validation, the invalid count and reasons are included in the summary log
Test verifies get_status() returns correct counts after init with mixed valid/invalid cookie files
Test verifies the summary log message is emitted during __init__
userStories.notes: Tier: S (small). DONE: Updated __init__ summary log to format 'Cookie rotator: X/N cookies valid (Y invalid)'. Added required keys (total, valid, invalid, cooldown, exhausted) to get_status() while preserving legacy keys. Invalid reasons logged when continue_on_partial=True. 5 new tests in TestInitDiagnostics class. All 43 tests pass.

userStories.title: Validate retry configuration bounds in VideoDownloader init
acceptanceCriteria: VideoDownloader.__init__ validates max_retries_per_video is in range [0, 20] and raises ValueError if not
VideoDownloader.__init__ validates retry_backoff is in range [1.0, 10.0] and raises ValueError if not
A warning is logged if total max backoff time (initial_delay * backoff^max_retries) exceeds 600 seconds
Test verifies ValueError raised for negative max_retries_per_video
Test verifies ValueError raised for retry_backoff below 1.0
Test verifies warning logged when computed max backoff exceeds threshold
userStories.notes: Implemented: Added validation block in VideoDownloader.__init__ (core.py ~line 299) that checks max_retries in [0,20] and retry_backoff in [1.0,10.0], raising ValueError for out-of-bounds. Logs warning when sum of retry_delay*backoff^i exceeds 600s. 7 tests added to TestRetryConfigValidation in test_downloader_retry.py. All 28 tests pass.

userStories.title: Deduplicate escalation trigger regex from category definitions
acceptanceCriteria: The combined trigger regex in EscalationManager is built dynamically from _TRIGGER_CATEGORIES patterns rather than a separate hardcoded regex
A startup assertion in __init__ verifies all patterns in _TRIGGER_CATEGORIES compile as valid regex
The `_categorize_error` method uses _TRIGGER_CATEGORIES as the single source of truth
Test verifies that all patterns from _TRIGGER_CATEGORIES match the combined regex
Test verifies that invalid regex patterns in _TRIGGER_CATEGORIES raise an error at init time
userStories.notes: Tier: M (medium). Source files: src/downloader/escalation_manager.py (lines 24-52 main regex, lines 54-68 _TRIGGER_CATEGORIES). Currently the main regex and category patterns are defined separately, meaning a 429 error can match both '429' and 'rate.?limit' patterns. Building from a single source prevents drift and ensures mutual exclusion.

userStories.title: Cap circuit breaker jitter to respect max_pause_seconds
acceptanceCriteria: The final pause duration after jitter application never exceeds max_pause_seconds
Jitter is applied before the max_pause_seconds cap in the calculation pipeline
Test verifies that with jitter_factor=0.5 and pause near max_pause_seconds, the result is capped at max_pause_seconds
Test verifies that jitter still applies when pause is well below max_pause_seconds
Existing circuit breaker tests continue to pass
userStories.notes: Tier: S (small). Source files: src/downloader/circuit_breaker.py (lines 265 _get_effective_pause_seconds caps before jitter, lines 269-286 _apply_jitter adds after). Currently jitter can push the total pause over max_pause_seconds by up to (jitter_factor * 100)%. Fix: apply cap after jitter, or apply jitter before cap in _get_effective_pause_seconds.

userStories.title: Clean up cooldown dict entries for removed cookies
acceptanceCriteria: CookieRotator._remove_invalid_cookie also removes the entry from _failed_cookies dict if present
CookieRotator._remove_invalid_cookie also removes the entry from _cooldown_until dict if present
Test verifies that after a cookie is marked failed then removed, _failed_cookies no longer contains that path
Test verifies that repeated fail+remove cycles do not grow the _failed_cookies dict unboundedly
Existing cookie rotator tests continue to pass
userStories.notes: Tier: S (small). Source files: src/downloader/cookie_rotator.py (lines 232-250 mark_failed, _remove_invalid_cookie). Currently when a failed cookie is removed from the active list, its cooldown timestamp remains in _failed_cookies dict. This is a memory leak: dict grows without bound if cookies keep failing and being removed. Fix is a 2-line cleanup in _remove_invalid_cookie.

userStories.title: Add batch-level diagnostics to match data restore
acceptanceCriteria: When match restore encounters multiple entries with empty source_file, a single summary warning is logged: '{N} match entries have empty source_file (likely all gap matches)'
Individual ValueError exceptions for empty source_file are suppressed when batch count exceeds 10
The summary includes a recommendation: 'Re-run MATCH stage with --match-only'
Test verifies that restoring 100 entries with empty source_file produces one summary log, not 100 individual errors
Test verifies that restoring entries with other invalid fields (e.g., non-string video_file) still raise individual errors
userStories.notes: Tier: M (medium). Source files: src/state.py (lines 125-127 restore validation), src/stages/match.py (lines 182-183 serialization). The interview notes describe 566 entries with empty source_file generating 566 individual ValueErrors. This overwhelms logs and obscures the root cause. Fix: collect empty-source_file errors, emit batch summary, keep individual errors for other validation failures.

userStories.title: Validate cookies_from_browser PATH availability at startup
acceptanceCriteria: During download subsystem initialization, if cookies_from_browser is set, shutil.which() checks the browser is on PATH
If the browser is not found, a clear warning is logged: 'cookies_from_browser is set to {browser} but it is not found on PATH. Cookie extraction will fail at Tier 3. Set cookies_path instead.'
The warning is emitted once at startup, not on every download attempt
Test verifies warning is logged when cookies_from_browser is set to a non-existent browser
Test verifies no warning when cookies_from_browser is set to an available browser
userStories.notes: Tier: S (small). Source files: src/downloader/core.py (VideoDownloader.__init__ or check_dependencies), src/config/sections/download.py (cookies_from_browser field). The interview notes specifically call out Firefox not being on PATH causing Tier 3 failures. A startup check prevents silent failures hours into a pipeline run. Use shutil.which() which is already imported in the codebase.

userStories.title: Document and extract timeout precedence constants in download core
acceptanceCriteria: The _run_download_cmd method has a docstring explaining the timeout selection precedence: (1) timeout_override param, (2) tier-specific download_timeouts, (3) config default, (4) adaptive multiplier
The 1.5x stall-to-max timeout multiplier at line ~2067-2068 is extracted to a named constant STALL_TO_MAX_TIMEOUT_RATIO with explanatory comment
The named constant is defined at module level or in DownloadConfig
Test verifies STALL_TO_MAX_TIMEOUT_RATIO is used (not a magic number) by checking the constant exists and is referenced
userStories.notes: Tier: S (small). Source files: src/downloader/core.py (lines 1996-2006 _run_download_cmd timeout logic, lines 2067-2068 magic 1.5x multiplier). Currently timeout logic has three sources of truth plus an adaptive multiplier with no documentation of precedence. The 1.5x multiplier relationship between stall timeout and max timeout is unexplained.

userStories.title: Add per-keyword strategy exhaustion tracking to rate limit budget
acceptanceCriteria: RateLimitBudget has a `keywords_exhausted_strategies` dict tracking which keywords have exhausted which strategies (cookies, vpn, impersonation)
When a keyword exhausts cookie rotations, subsequent calls to should_attempt_strategy('cookies', keyword) return False for that keyword
Other keywords are not affected by one keyword's exhaustion
Test verifies that keyword A exhausting cookies does not block keyword B from trying cookies
Test verifies that per-keyword exhaustion persists across retry attempts for the same keyword
Existing rate limit budget tests continue to pass
userStories.notes: Tier: M (medium). Source files: src/downloader/rate_limit_budget.py (RateLimitBudget class), src/downloader/core.py (lines 449-485 _share_budget_across_keywords). Currently when one keyword exhausts cookie rotations, subsequent keywords also skip cookies even though the rotator might work for different search terms. Keywords processed earlier unfairly consume more budget.

userStories.title: Enrich download subprocess error context with command metadata
acceptanceCriteria: When a yt-dlp subprocess fails, the error log includes: (1) which call site triggered it (keyword search, ID download, audio, segment, caption), (2) the current escalation tier, (3) whether impersonation was active
The call site identifier is passed as a `context` parameter to _run_download_cmd
Error classification in error_classification.py receives the context metadata for enriched error categorization
Test verifies that error logs from different call sites include the correct context identifier
Test verifies that the context parameter is optional for backward compatibility
userStories.notes: Tier: M (medium). Source files: src/downloader/core.py (_run_download_cmd at ~line 1996, 8 call sites listed in prompt.md), src/downloader/error_classification.py. Currently when a subprocess fails, the error log doesn't indicate which of the 8 call sites triggered it. Adding context helps diagnose whether failures are keyword-search-specific, download-specific, or caption-specific. The context parameter should be optional with default None.
